info.title: PulsHealth Product API
info.summary: Read-only HTTP API over the health data a PulsHealth server holds.
info.description:
Read-only JSON API over the HealthKit data your iPhone synced into your own PulsHealth server: daily metrics, activity rings, workouts and their streams, sleep, raw samples, State of Mind, a chat-ready summary and bulk export.

Every data route needs `Authorization: Bearer <PULS_API_TOKEN>` and answers for one user. Timestamps are epoch milliseconds, ranges are half-open `[start, end)`, and day-grained answers use the selected account's reporting calendar (falling back to `PULS_TIME_ZONE`). Errors are `{"error": "..."}` with a conventional status code.

Guide: https://pulshealth.com/docs/api/

externalDocs.description: Guide: authentication, conventions, paging and errors

get.description: A JSON index pointing at the documentation, the OpenAPI document and the health check.
A self-contained HTML reference served by the deployment itself. The full documentation is at https://pulshealth.com/docs/api/.

This document. `servers[0].url` is the base URL the request arrived on, so a client generator or a ChatGPT Action imports it as is. Behind a proxy that host comes from `X-Forwarded-Host` only with `TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=true`.
Liveness for a container health check. The database status is cached for two seconds, so polling it never holds a database connection.

200.description: The service and its database are up.

get.description: Every user with the gate on (`PULS_MULTI_USER=true`); only the default user with it off. `default` is the user served when a request names none (`PULS_USER_ID`); `multiUser` says whether ?user= may name anyone else. `timeZone` is the selected account's reporting zone; each user also carries its own `timeZone`. Raw daily grouping uses this zone; uploaded ring and aggregate local dates are preserved.
The HealthKit characteristics the phone uploaded for this user: name, e-mail, date of birth and biological sex.

Every type with at least one row for this user, raw or aggregate, with its kind, canonical unit, row counts and time span. Counting rows is expensive, so the answer is cached per user for five minutes. After that the cached answer is still served, for up to an hour, while one background refresh replaces it, so new uploads can take a little longer than five minutes to appear; only a user's first request waits for the count.
The newest raw sample of each requested quantity type. Types with no data are left out, so the list can be shorter than `types`.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated HealthKit quantity identifiers, at most 50.

get.description: One value per local calendar day (in the selected account's reporting zone) for each requested type, every day overlapping `[start, end)`. Paged in days across the requested types: `limit` and `offset` count day rows, not metrics, in the order the response nests them (the requested types in request order, each ascending by day); `nextOffset` is `offset` plus the rows on the page and a page shorter than `limit` is the last. The default page holds a year of 27 types.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated HealthKit identifiers, at most 50; the response keeps this order.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Day rows per page, across all requested types; larger values are clamped.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page; a page with fewer day rows than `limit` means the end.

400.description: Missing types or range, or an invalid `limit` or `offset`.

get.description: One row per local calendar day overlapping `[start, end)`, as the Fitness app shows the rings.
Workouts newest first, optionally limited to `[start, end)` on the start time and to one activity type.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Only workouts starting at or after this instant. Epoch milliseconds.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: Only workouts starting before this instant. Epoch milliseconds.

parameters.name: activityType
parameters.description: Only this HealthKit activity type, e.g. `running`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Workouts per page; larger values are clamped.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page; a page shorter than `limit` is the last.

400.description: An invalid range, limit or offset.

get.description: One workout with HealthKit's per-type statistics, its events and, for a multisport workout, its activities.
Per-second curves recorded during the workout, each downsampled to at most `maxPoints` points by bucket-averaging while keeping the first and last point.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated HealthKit identifiers, at most 50; omit for every recorded stream.

parameters.name: maxPoints
parameters.description: Points per stream after downsampling; larger values are clamped.

get.description: One row per sleep session, attributed to the local calendar day it ended on. Sessions are split on gaps over three hours, and every local day overlapping `[start, end)` is covered.

400.description: Invalid range, or a range over 366 days.

get.description: Individual HealthKit records, ordered by start time, not deduplicated across devices. The range is `[start, end)` on the sample start time and may not exceed 31 days.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Samples per page; larger values are clamped.

400.description: Unknown type, a non-sample type, or a range over 31 days.

get.description: Entries whose instant falls on a local calendar day overlapping `[start, end)`, oldest first. At most 366 days per request.

400.description: Invalid range, or a range over 366 days.

get.description: The last range calendar days (7d by default; ending today in the selected account's reporting zone) as one markdown page of under sixty lines, meant to be pasted into a chat that has no MCP connection: a header naming the user, the days and the zone, then a section for each kind of data that exists — activity (steps, active energy, exercise minutes, stand hours as daily means and totals), heart (resting heart rate, HRV), sleep (time asleep per night), workouts (count, total time, distance, most frequent activities), body (newest weight and body fat) — and a coverage line (last sync, days with data, and the reminder that daily figures are already deduplicated across devices). Every figure comes from the daily surfaces the other endpoints serve, never from raw samples. `format=json` returns the same numbers as a Summary object.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How many calendar days, ending today, the summary covers.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: markdown for the page (text/markdown), json for the Summary object it is rendered from.

400.description: A range or format outside the accepted values.

get.description: Streams a whole range as a file (`Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Content-Disposition: attachment`) instead of a JSON document. CSV opens the file with a header row; JSONL writes one JSON object per line whose keys are the same column names. Field names match the JSON endpoints; where an endpoint nests (a metric's days, a night's stages) the export flattens, repeating the identifying fields on every row and naming a nested field by its path. Ranges are capped at 31 days for samples (as `/v1/samples` is) and 366 days for every other dataset — the same cap `/v1/sleep/daily` and `/v1/state-of-mind` apply, and deliberately stricter than `/v1/metrics/daily` and `/v1/workouts`, which are bounded by a page size rather than by their range, and `/v1/activity/summary`, which is one small row per day. The `daily_metrics` and workouts datasets return the whole range (workouts newest first); `limit` and `offset` are not used here. At most 2 exports run at once, because each holds a database connection for the length of the download; over that is a 503 with `Retry-After`. An export ends after 30 minutes, and one whose client stops reading for a minute is dropped; either way the connection is aborted, so the file is a visibly failed download rather than a short one. The 30-second query limit of the other routes does not apply.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: `csv` for a spreadsheet (header row first), `jsonl` for one JSON object per line.

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: Which rows to export. Each dataset's columns are the matching JSON endpoint's field names.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: `daily_metrics` only, and required there: comma-separated HealthKit identifiers, at most 50.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: samples only, and required there: exactly one HealthKit identifier.

parameters.name: activityType
parameters.description: workouts only: keep one activity type.

200.description: The dataset, streamed as an attachment named puls-<dataset>-<start>-<end>.<`csv`|`jsonl`>.

400.description: Missing or invalid format or dataset, a missing dataset parameter, an unknown type, or a range over the dataset's cap.

503.description: Too many exports already in progress; retry after the `Retry-After` interval.

bearerAuth.description: `PULS_API_TOKEN` from the server's `.env`. Not the phone's ingest token.

User.name: user
User.description: The user to answer for. Defaults to the deployment's `PULS_USER_ID`. Naming anyone else needs `PULS_MULTI_USER=true`, otherwise the answer is `403`. `GET /v1/users` lists them.

Start.name: start
Start.description: Inclusive start of the range, in epoch milliseconds.

End.name: end
End.description: Exclusive end of the range, in epoch milliseconds. Must be after `start`.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Rows to skip. Pass the previous page's `nextOffset`.

BadRequest.description: A parameter is missing, malformed or out of range. The message names it.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token is missing or wrong. Counts against the failed-authentication limit.

Forbidden.description: `user` names someone other than the default user while `PULS_MULTI_USER` is off.

NotFound.description: Nothing with that identifier exists for this user.

TooManyRequests.description: Too many failed authentications from this client address. The request was refused before the token was checked.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until the next attempt will be evaluated.

InternalError.description: The query failed. Details are in the server log, never in the response.

GatewayTimeout.description: The query ran past its 30-second limit and was cancelled (`{"error": "query took too long; narrow the range"}`). Narrow the range or page smaller.

name.description: Name from the phone's profile, if set.

email.description: E-mail from the phone's profile, if set.

dateOfBirth.description: Date of birth as epoch milliseconds at UTC midnight.

timeZone.description: The account reporting IANA time zone, falling back to PULS_TIME_ZONE for accounts without a preference. Calendar ranges and raw daily grouping use this zone; uploaded ring and aggregate dates retain their recorded local day.

Profile.description: The HealthKit characteristics the phone last uploaded. Fields the person never filled in are null.

User.description: One user the deployment answers for, with what the batches log says about their uploads.

userID.description: The user's id. Pass it as `user=` on any `/v1` route.

name.description: Name from the phone's profile, if set.

email.description: E-mail from the phone's profile, if set.

createdAt.description: When the server first saw this user. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

lastSync.description: Epoch milliseconds of the most recent batch; null when nothing has been uploaded.

uploadedSamples.description: Sum of the sample counts the batches declared.

timeZone.description: The account reporting IANA time zone, falling back to PULS_TIME_ZONE for accounts without a preference. Calendar ranges and raw daily grouping use this zone; uploaded ring and aggregate dates retain their recorded local day.

unit.description: Canonical unit every value of the type is stored in; null for types without one.

aggregateRows.description: Aggregate buckets the phone computed (what daily metrics are built from).

earliest.description: Start of the oldest row. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

latest.description: Start of the newest row. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

CatalogType.description: One HealthKit type that holds data for this user.

timestamp.description: Start of the sample. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

LatestMetric.description: The newest raw sample of one quantity type.

DailyMetric.description: One type's local-day series, deduplicated across devices. A page boundary can fall inside days, so the same identifier may open the next page; append its days.

date.description: Local calendar day in the account reporting zone; uploaded aggregate dates preserve their recorded day.

value.description: The day's total for a cumulative type (steps), its mean for a discrete one (heart rate).

moveMode.description: HealthKit move mode: 1 active energy, 2 move time.

ActivityDay.description: One day of Activity rings. A ring the device does not track is null.

distanceM.description: Total distance, metres; null when none was recorded.

hasRoute.description: Whether GPS route points were synced.

routePointCount.description: Number of GPS route points synced for this workout.

isIndoor.description: Whether HealthKit metadata (`HKIndoorWorkout`) explicitly marks this workout as indoor (`true`) or outdoor (`false`). Omitted when the metadata key was not recorded.

elevationAscendedM.description: Total elevation ascended in metres (`HKElevationAscended`) when present in HealthKit workout metadata.

availableMetrics.description: HealthKit identifiers with a stream in `GET /v1/workouts/{uuid}/series`.

WorkoutSummary.description: One workout, without its streams or events.

statisticsDetail.description: Per-type statistics HealthKit computed for the workout, keyed by HealthKit identifier, in each type's canonical unit.

events.description: Workout events (pauses, laps, segments) as HealthKit reported them.

SleepStages.description: Minutes per stage, from the single source that recorded the most sleep. `asleepMinutes` is core + deep + rem + unspecified; awake is time awake during the session and is not part of it.

SleepNight.description: One sleep session, attributed to the local calendar day it ended on (the wake-up day). Overlapping sources are never summed: `inBedMinutes` is the highest single-source total and `asleepMinutes` plus stages come from the source with the most sleep.

start.description: First sample of the session, any source. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

end.description: Last sample of the session, any source. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

asleepMinutes.description: Core + deep + REM + unspecified of the winning source, minutes.

sources.description: Distinct sources that contributed samples to this session.

value.description: Quantity value in the page's canonical unit, or the category type's integer enum value.

label.description: Category types only: the HealthKit name of value.

source.description: Name of the app or device that recorded it.

SamplesPage.description: Raw HealthKit samples of one type, ordered by start time. Not deduplicated across devices.

unit.description: Canonical unit of every quantity value; null for category types.

nextOffset.description: Offset to pass for the next page; a short page means the end.

points.description: [epoch milliseconds, value] pairs, ordered by time.

maxPoints.description: The point cap applied to each stream.

date.description: Local calendar day of the entry.

timestamp.description: When it was logged. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

valenceClassification.description: Apple's band for valence, e.g. slightlyPleasant.

associations.description: What they are about, e.g. work, family.

SummaryStat.description: One daily series over the summary's range: the days that had a value and the mean, minimum and maximum of those days. total is present for cumulative series only (steps, energy, exercise minutes). source names the table the values came from.

SummaryReading.description: The newest raw sample of a body metric, whenever it was taken.

timestamp.description: When the reading was taken. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

Summary.description: GET `/v1/summary`?`format=json`: the numbers behind the markdown page. A section is absent when the range holds no data for it.

endDate.description: Last local calendar day covered: today in timeZone.

generatedAt.description: When the summary was computed. Epoch milliseconds (UTC).

timeZone.description: The selected account reporting IANA zone, falling back to PULS_TIME_ZONE.

sleep.description: The longest sleep session of each wake-up day in the range.

totalDistanceM.description: Absent when no workout in the range recorded a distance.

byActivityType.description: Most frequent first, at most three.

lastSync.description: Epoch milliseconds of the most recent upload; null when nothing has been uploaded.

daysWithData.description: Days in the range on which at least one section has a value.

Error.description: Every non-2xx answer from a JSON route.

error.description: What went wrong, in English. Meant for a person or a log, not for matching.

examples: Optional ?user=<uuid> on every /v1 route selects the user (default PULS_USER_ID; others need PULS_MULTI_USER=true); GET /v1/users lists them.
Read-only API for downstream products that use PulsHealth data.

db.description: Whether the database answered a ping in the last two seconds.

default.description: The user served when a request names none (`PULS_USER_ID`).

timeZone.description: Reporting IANA time zone of the selected user (?user=, otherwise the default). Each users entry also exposes its own reporting zone.
